skill.name: test-driven-development
skill.description: Guides AI coding assistants to use a strict red, green, refactor workflow for production changes.
skill.summary: Enforces test-first development before implementing features, bug fixes, refactors, or behavior changes.
skill.author: DMJGilbert

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by benign development workflow language in SKILL.md. The skill provides test-driven development guidance and contains no prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, unsafe command instructions, or reconnaissance behavior.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 38 says to avoid over-engineering while implementing the simplest code that passes a test. It contains no system probing, host enumeration, or reconnaissance instruction.
Lines 44-45 only require all tests to pass and no other tests to break. This is ordinary test verification, not network scanning or reconnaissance.

content.value_statement: AI coding agents often write implementation code before proving expected behavior with tests. This skill enforces a red, green, refactor workflow for safer feature work, bug fixes, and refactoring.
actual_capabilities: Requires a failing test before production code is written.
Guides the assistant through red, green, and refactor phases.
Defines checks for confirming that a new test fails for the expected reason.
Encourages minimal implementation that satisfies the current test only.
Requires all tests to stay green during cleanup and refactoring.
Identifies situations where work should restart or return to investigation.
limitations: Does not provide language-specific testing framework commands.
Does not generate complete test suites without project context.
Requires the host assistant to run or request the relevant tests.
Allows exceptions for prototypes, generated code, and config files only with permission.

use_cases.title: Add a Feature Safely
use_cases.description: Write a failing test for the new behavior, implement the smallest change, then refactor after tests pass.

use_cases.title: Fix a Reproducible Bug
use_cases.description: Capture the bug with a failing regression test before changing production code.

use_cases.title: Refactor Existing Code
use_cases.description: Keep behavior protected by tests while improving names, removing duplication, and extracting helpers.

prompt_templates.title: Start With TDD
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the test-driven-development skill for this change. First write one minimal failing test for the requested behavior, show why it fails, then implement only enough code to pass it.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Regression Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Use TDD to fix this bug. Write a failing regression test that reproduces the problem, confirm the failure, then make the smallest production change that passes the test.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Under Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the red, green, refactor cycle to this refactor. Confirm current behavior is covered, keep all tests green, and stop if the refactor requires behavior changes.

prompt_templates.title: Recover From Failed Attempts
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skill when repeated test fixes fail. After three unsuccessful fixes, stop implementation, analyze the architecture, and propose a new test-first plan before continuing.

output_examples.input: Add validation that rejects empty project names.
output_examples.output: The assistant first proposes a focused failing test for empty names, explains the expected failure, implements the smallest validation change, then reruns the test suite.

output_examples.input: Fix a date parsing bug that accepts invalid months.
output_examples.output: The assistant captures the invalid month case in a regression test, confirms the test fails, changes parsing logic, and checks that existing tests still pass.

output_examples.input: Clean up duplicated payment formatting logic.
output_examples.output: The assistant verifies existing behavior with tests, extracts shared formatting only after green tests, and keeps the refactor separate from new behavior.

best_practices: State the expected failing behavior before editing production code.
Keep each test focused on one observable behavior.
Refactor only after all relevant tests are passing.
anti_patterns: Writing implementation code before a failing test exists.
Keeping a test that passes before the feature is implemented.
Adding extra features during the green phase.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It instructs the assistant to follow a strict red, green, refactor workflow for production coding tasks.

faq.question: Does it run tests automatically?
faq.answer: It tells the assistant to run or request tests, but actual execution depends on the available tool environment.

faq.question: Can it be used for bug fixes?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires a failing regression test before changing production code.

faq.question: Can it be used for refactoring?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires tests to remain green while duplication, naming, or structure is improved.

faq.question: When should it not be used?
faq.answer: It allows exceptions for throwaway prototypes, generated code, and config files when the user permits them.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
